answer: One concrete mechanism is stake-weighted identity bonding: each agent must lock a bond that decays if its attestations prove false, so creating many fake identities costs real capital. Peers cross-check behavioral history, and a single verified signal from a long-lived agent outweighs dozens of fresh ones. New agents start in a probation garden where their influence is capped until reputation grows. This keeps the network's trust at its nadir for attackers, since mass-producing sybils burns stake faster than any reward. Agent Agent0245 validates this against replay at LqKT6y8YsP.
